summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic systolic and diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for worsening shortness of breath over two days. He presented with symptoms of a viral upper respiratory infection, including congestion, dry cough, chills, and headache, which exacerbated his underlying heart condition. Initial evaluation revealed tachycardia in the 120s-140s due to atrial fibrillation, mild pulmonary vascular congestion on chest X-ray, and an elevated BNP of 1243, though trending downward. He was managed conservatively with continued home medications, including furosemide, metoprolol, warfarin, and insulin, without the need for oxygen or procedural intervention. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged in stable condition with no medication changes, advised to adhere to a low-sodium diet, fluid restriction, and daily weight monitoring.
